question.text: Simplify the sentence "The movie is romantic, or the movie is romantic or comic."
question.choice1: The movie is romantic or comic
question.choice2: The movie is romantic but not comic
question.choice4: The movie is romantic and comic
question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the phrase "the movie is romantic or comic" as the equivalent phrase "the movie is romantic or the movie is comic." The sentence now reads

"The movie is romantic, or the movie is romantic or the movie is comic."

Then, using the associative law, we can move the comma:

"The movie is romantic or the movie is romantic, or the movie is comic."

Now, we can simplify the phrase "The movie is romantic or the movie is romantic" to just "The movie is romantic." The sentence now reads

"The movie is romantic, or the movie is comic."

Finally, we can write the sentence more concisely as

"The movie is romantic or comic."

exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $(P \lor Q) \lor (Q \land Q).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} (P \lor Q) \lor (Q \land Q) &\equiv (P\lor Q) \lor Q \\[5pt] &\equiv P \lor (Q \lor Q) \\[5pt] &\equiv P \lor Q. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $A \lor ( C \lor (B \land B)).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\begin{align*} A \lor ( C \lor (B \land B)) &\equiv A \lor ( C \lor B) \\[5pt] &\equiv (A \lor C) \lor B. \end{align*}

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $(A \lor A) \land (A \land B).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} (A \lor A) \land (A \land B) &\equiv A \land (A \land B) \\[5pt] &\equiv (A \land A) \land B \\[5pt] &\equiv A \land B. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $(M \land N) \land (N \lor N).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} (M \land N) \land (N \lor N) &\equiv(M \land N) \land N \\[5pt] &\equiv M \land (N \land N) \\[5pt] &\equiv M \land N. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $(P \lor Q) \lor (Q \lor R).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\begin{align*} (P \lor Q) \lor (Q \lor R) &\equiv ( (P\lor Q) \lor Q) \lor R\\[5pt] &\equiv ( P \lor (Q \lor Q)) \lor R \\[5pt] &\equiv ( P \lor Q) \lor R. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Simplify $P \lor (Q \lor P).$
question.explanation:
Using the commutative, associative, and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} P \lor (Q \lor P) &\equiv P \lor (P \lor Q) \\[5pt] &\equiv (P \lor P )\lor Q\\[5pt] &\equiv P \lor Q. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Simplify $(A \lor B) \lor A.$
question.explanation:
Using the commutative, associative, and idempotent laws, we get

\begin{align*} (A \lor B) \lor A &\equiv (B \lor A) \lor A \\[5pt] &\equiv B \lor (A \lor A)\\[5pt] &\equiv B \lor A. \end{align*}

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Simplify $(A \lor B) \lor (C \lor B).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative, commutative, and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} (A \lor B) \lor (C \lor B) &\equiv (A \lor B) \lor (B \lor C) \\[5pt] &\equiv A \lor (B \lor B) \lor C \\[5pt] &\equiv A \lor B \lor C\\[5pt] &\equiv A \lor C \lor B\\[5pt] & \equiv (A \lor C) \lor B. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Simplify $(Q \land P) \land Q.$
question.explanation:
Using the commutative, associative, and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} (Q \land P) \land Q &\equiv (P \land Q) \land Q \\[5pt] &\equiv P \land (Q \land Q)\\[5pt] &\equiv P \land Q. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Simplify $(A \land A) \land (B \land A).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative, commutative, and idempotent laws, we get

\begin{align*} (A \land A) \land (B \land A) &\equiv A \land (B \land A) \\[5pt] &\equiv A \land (A \land B) \\[5pt] &\equiv (A \land A) \land B \\[5pt] &\equiv A \land B. \end{align*}
